---
title: "surveyframe and surveydown"
description: "How surveyframe relates to surveydown: what each does, what surveyframe adds for research, and how to analyse surveydown responses with surveyframe."
---

surveydown is an open-source R package (MIT, on CRAN) for programmable surveys written in markdown and R, built on Quarto and shiny. It stores respondent data in a PostgreSQL database.

surveyframe is a free R package (MIT, on CRAN) for the whole research workflow around a survey: the questionnaire and its analysis plan, the collection, the checks, the planned analyses and the APA 7 report.

## What the surveyframe workflow provides

- An analysis plan written before the data, with hypotheses and decision
  rules, saved in the questionnaire file.
- A pre-analysis plan to submit to OSF, Zenodo or an ethics committee.
- A hash anyone can check at [surveyframe.org/verify](https://surveyframe.org/verify/),
  and amendments recorded with their reasons.
- Quality checks, scale reliability, the planned analyses and a report in
  APA 7, in SurveyStudio or in R.

## Using surveydown with surveyframe

You can collect responses with surveydown and analyse them with surveyframe. Describe the questionnaire as a surveyframe instrument, then prepare the export so that `read_responses()` can check it against the instrument:

1. Read the responses from your PostgreSQL database into a data frame, as surveydown's documentation shows.
2. Give each question in surveydown the id of the matching surveyframe item, or name each column by its item id after reading.
3. Declare any column outside the instrument, such as the session id or the time, in `meta_cols`.

```r
raw <- data  # the responses read from your database
names(raw) <- c("submitted", "visit_type", "satisfaction")  # each column named by its item id, in order
raw$visit_type <- c("First visit" = "first", "Returning" = "returning")[raw$visit_type]  # answer text to choice codes, where needed
responses <- read_responses(raw, instrument, meta_cols = "submitted")
results <- run_analysis_plan(responses, instrument)
```

The planned analyses and the report then run on these responses.
